summary: LLM inference costs scale linearly with token usage, and most production applications waste 50-80% of their spend on redundant context, oversized models, and uncached repeated requests. By combining prompt caching, model routing, and semantic caching, teams routinely cut API bills by 50-90% while simultaneously reducing latency. These are inference-time optimizations that require no model retraining and can often be deployed in days.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Cache the static prefix of prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, documents) so providers skip reprocessing repeated input tokens. Cached input tokens are billed at a steep discount or served from a lower-latency path.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your long, unchanging system prompt and RAG context at the start of the message and enable cache_control (Anthropic) or rely on automatic prefix caching (OpenAI) so repeated calls only pay full price for the dynamic user question.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store previous query-response pairs and serve a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (via embedding similarity), avoiding an LLM call entirely. Typical production hit rates reach ~68%.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming questions; if cosine similarity to a stored question exceeds 0.95, return the cached response instead of calling the API.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Cascading
techniques.description: Route easy requests to small, cheap models and escalate only hard requests to larger, expensive ones. A cascade tries a cheap model first and falls back to a stronger model if confidence or validation fails.
techniques.example: Send classification and simple extraction tasks to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku, and only route ambiguous or high-stakes queries to GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet using LiteLLM or a RouteLLM classifier.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim redundant words, boilerplate, and verbose few-shot examples, and compress context using tools that remove low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Replace a 10-example few-shot prompt with 3 well-chosen examples, or run context through LLMLingua to compress a 2,000-token document into ~600 tokens before sending it.

techniques.name: Max Tokens & Output Control
techniques.description: Output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens, so capping max_tokens and instructing concise responses directly lowers cost and latency.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Answer in one sentence' to the prompt, or request structured JSON to eliminate conversational filler.

techniques.name: Retrieval Context Pruning (RAG optimization)
techniques.description: Retrieve and inject only the most relevant chunks instead of dumping entire documents, using reranking and top-k limits to shrink context length.
techniques.example: Instead of passing 20 retrieved chunks, use a cross-encoder reranker (e.g. Cohere Rerank) to select the top 3-5 chunks that actually answer the query.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batch job, which providers price at a significant discount for non-real-time workloads.
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk classification or summarization jobs through the OpenAI Batch API or Anthropic Message Batches API to get ~50% off standard rates.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as a stop sequence or sufficient answer is reached, avoiding paying for unnecessary trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '###' so generation halts after the structured answer instead of rambling to max_tokens.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned Small Models for Repetitive Tasks
techniques.description: For narrow, high-volume tasks, a small fine-tuned or distilled model matches larger-model quality at a fraction of the per-token cost and latency.
techniques.example: Distill a repetitive support-ticket categorization task from GPT-4o into a fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini or a self-hosted Llama 3.1 8B model.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to avoid duplicate API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for underlying vector store/infra

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache (RedisVL)
tools.description: Semantic caching built on Redis vector search that serves cached LLM responses for semantically similar queries with low latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo, enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering model routing, fallback, load balancing, caching, and spend tracking behind one OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LiteLLM Enterprise from custom pricing (~$250+/mo tiers)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing logging, caching, rate limiting, cost analytics, and prompt management via a proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from $20/mo (Pro) with usage-based scaling

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), model routing, and RAG components to reduce redundant calls.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that reduces prompt length by up to 20x while preserving key information for the model.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and observability across 250+ models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free dev tier; paid plans from $49/mo and enterprise custom

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace that routes requests across many model providers, enabling easy price-based model selection and fallback.
tools.pricing_paid: Pass-through per-token pricing plus a small platform fee

tools.name: Cohere Rerank
tools.description: Reranking API that scores and reorders retrieved documents so you can pass fewer, more relevant chunks to the LLM and cut context tokens.
tools.pricing_paid: Usage-based, ~$2 per 1,000 search units; free trial keys available

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching and move all static system prompts and context to the start of your messages to save up to 90% on repeated input tokens.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to eliminate duplicate and near-duplicate requests entirely.
Route simple requests to a cheap model (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash) and reserve premium models for hard queries.
Cap max_tokens and instruct concise/JSON outputs, since output tokens cost 2-4x more than input tokens.
Trim prompt bloat: cut excess few-shot examples and prune RAG context to only the top 3-5 reranked chunks.
